A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
strontium isotopy is an excellent tracer for understanding hydrologic and paleo-hydrologic processes in this region.

the strontium isotope system provides useful information on hydrologic processes in the Altiplanos, especially when combined with major-element budgets, and that the isotopic system is not in steady state, even in the modern system.

strontium isotopically derived mass balances provide a useful complement to the major-element budgets and can help constrain the paleohydrologic and paleoclimatic evolution of the central Andean Altiplano.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the isotopic composition of riverine inputs to Lake Titicaca has been relatively stable over the past 10 000 years, but that the lake has been in isotopic disequilibrium with respect to its inputs for most of that time.
strontium isotopy can be used to improve hydrologic mass balances in closed-basin lakes, which in turn can be used to better understand the climatic history of arid regions.
strontium isotopy can provide important information about paleohydrologic changes, but the information is not always as straightforward as one would like.
